result:
The O3 lesson is written, with a quiz, its key and a cheat sheet. I didn't open the lesson in a browser and didn't count its words. I estimate about 4,000 words, inside the 2,700 to 6,750 range for 30 minutes.

- **Lesson:** `lessons/0001-context-and-memory.html`. It opens with the win: say what the makerspace assistant sees at each step, what it forgets between visits, and when to use context, notes or retrieval.
  - It covers the context window and context rot, why the program re-sends the whole transcript on every call, and why nothing carries over between sessions.
  - It also covers notes and compaction, and retrieval: chunking, embeddings, BM25, and chunks that lose their machine name.
  - It has three figures, practice checks with instant feedback, and a worked token-cost example (12,500 input tokens for one request). A faded version follows, then a "design it" exercise.
- **Sources:** the lesson draws on two Anthropic pages I opened and read, [Effective context engineering for AI agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents) (the primary source) and [Introducing Contextual Retrieval](https://www.anthropic.com/news/contextual-retrieval). Both are in `RESOURCES.md`.
- **Quiz and key:** `quizzes/0002.json` and `keys/0002.json`, five items with none repeating the lesson's practice.
- **Cheat sheet:** `cheatsheets/context-and-memory.html`.
- **Notes:** `NOTES.md` now records the new misconception id M7 (a big window means context needs no curation). It also records that quiz 0001's two submissions are still ungraded.

I didn't write a learning record, since there's no new evidence of what you've learned yet.

I found no community I could verify, so the lesson suggests testing the ideas at your team's design review instead. I can look for one if you want.

The quiz is ready whenever you are, and you can ask me about any part of the lesson.
